headline: GOLD BREAKS $4,100 — Split Fed Holds Rates 9-3 With Three Hawks Pushing for Hike; US Pauses Iran Airstrikes Overnight
snippet: Gold recovered sharply from a brief dip below the $4,000 psychological threshold to break above $4,100 on July 31, driven by the Federal Reserve's 9-3 vote on July 30 to hold rates at 3.50%–3.75% — with Cleveland, Minneapolis, and Dallas Fed presidents all dissenting in favour of an immediate 25-basis-point hike — and overnight news that the U.S. paused airstrikes on Iranian military targets. Mining equities responded: Wheaton Precious Metals gained 1.1% and Franco-Nevada 2.4% on the announcement. For junior mining investors who rode out gold's sub-$4,000 scare, the snap-back confirms that a Fed divided on inflation, combined with an active U.S.-Iran conflict now entering its sixth month, creates a structurally resilient safe-haven bid that is likely to support gold's autumn seasonality setup.

headline: KOREA + CHILE LOCK IN MINERAL ALLIANCE — 5 MOUs Create Ministerial Lithium and Copper Pipeline; Seoul Calls Santiago "Natural and Ideal Partner"
snippet: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and Chilean President José Antonio Kast signed five memoranda of understanding on July 30 — the first Korean presidential visit to Chile in 11 years — including a Mineral Resources Partnership that elevates joint cooperation to the ministerial level and creates a new director-general-level working channel spanning the entire critical mineral supply chain from lithium brine to copper concentrate. Chile holds the world's largest lithium reserves and is the world's largest copper producer; South Korea is a global leader in EV battery manufacturing and semiconductors. For junior mining companies developing copper and lithium projects in Chile's Atacama and Antofagasta regions, the formalised institutional relationship signals growing South Korean offtake and strategic capital interest as an alternative to Chinese-dominated downstream processing.

headline: HECLA KENO HILL: 62.7 oz/ton Ag OVER 10.2 FEET — Bermingham Deep Trend Extended 800 Feet; Midas Adds Two New Blind Veins (NYSE: HL)
snippet: Hecla Mining Company (NYSE: HL) released Q2 2026 exploration results on July 29 confirming the Bermingham Deep high-grade silver trend at Keno Hill, Yukon has been extended 165 feet in both strike directions: hole 935C returned 62.7 oz/ton silver over 10.2 feet and hole 936C returned 44.6 oz/ton silver over 10.1 feet, with the Footwall Vein yielding 138.0 oz/ton silver over 3.1 feet. The trend is now traceable over 800 feet of strike, extending toward the historic Hector-Calumet Mine. At Midas in Nevada, two new blind veins were intersected in the Sinter–Pogo Gap target area. At $59 silver, Bermingham Deep's 62.7 oz/ton intercepts represent exceptional in-situ silver value that strengthens the case for resource growth at Hecla's flagship Canadian silver asset.

headline: $104M HEAVY RARE EARTH PLANT BREAKS GROUND IN UTAH — Energy Fuels Targets First US Commercial Terbium + Dysprosium Production by 2027 (UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU; TSX: EFR) announced on July 29 that construction has begun on a $104 million expansion of its White Mesa Mill in Utah — the first commercial-scale heavy rare earth oxide facility in the United States. Phase 1 targets up to 20 tonnes per year of terbium oxide and 120 tonnes per year of dysprosium oxide by end-2027, with feedstock from the Donald Project monazite in Australia and government cost-sharing support. The project addresses a direct supply crisis: dysprosium prices have surged approximately eightfold and terbium fivefold since China imposed export controls in April 2025, and Chinese shipments of both elements to Japan have been at zero for months. Energy Fuels is one of the only companies globally with operating uranium and rare earth production capability at a single facility.

headline: MINTO MINE NEARLY TRIPLES: SELKIRK COPPER M&I Copper +182% to 940Mlb — 47.8Mt Yukon Resource Sets Up 2028 Restart Bid (TSXV: SCMI)
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines Inc. (TSXV: SCMI) published an updated Mineral Resource Estimate on July 30 for the Minto copper-gold-silver project in the Yukon — a past-producing mine with established road, power, and port infrastructure — showing Measured and Indicated Resources of 47.8 million tonnes at 0.89% copper, 0.34 g/t gold, and 3.2 g/t silver, representing a 280% increase in tonnage and 182% increase in contained M&I copper to 940 million pounds versus the 2025 estimate. The result of a 52,288-metre Phase 1 drill program, the updated MRE also found significant new zone and open-pit potential not captured in prior estimates. Management targets a mid-2028 restart at copper prices above $5.00/lb; at the current $6.44/lb, the project economics are materially different than the original acquisition case.

headline: INDEPENDENCE GOLD FINDS THIRD BLIND VEIN AT 3Ts — Dixie Discovery Returns 2.80 g/t Au over 11.4m in BC Epithermal District (TSXV: IGO)
snippet: Independence Gold Corp. (TSXV: IGO) announced the discovery of the Dixie Vein — the third blind epithermal gold-silver vein found using the company's structural exploration model at its 100%-owned 3Ts Project in central British Columbia — with discovery hole 3TS-26-29 returning 11.40 metres grading 2.80 g/t gold and 12.54 g/t silver, including 1.99 metres at 6.94 g/t gold. The Dixie Vein follows the Balrog (announced June 29) and Goofy discoveries (announced July 22, which returned 14.70 g/t gold over 9.10 metres) from the same 10,000-metre spring drill program across the 35,486-hectare Nechako Plateau property. Three successful blind vein discoveries from one structural model across a district is a strong validation signal; with assays still pending across follow-up holes at all three veins, the 3Ts district story is still early in its development.

headline: MOTLEY FOOL PICKS 2 RARE EARTH STOCKS TO BUY, 1 TO SELL — As Dysprosium Hits 8x Pre-Controls Price and Beijing's Entity List Targets US Producers
snippet: The Motley Fool published rare earth stock picks on July 29, naming two rare earth mining companies as buys and one as a sell as Chinese export controls keep dysprosium prices near eightfold their pre-controls level and terbium near fivefold, while Beijing's June 22 entity-listing of MP Materials and USA Rare Earth adds operational risk for US-headquartered producers. The analysis reflects mainstream attention arriving late to a sector that has already had dramatic moves — with MP Materials, USA Rare Earth, and Lynas Rare Earths all seeing significant re-ratings — and signals that retail inflows may begin to reach smaller rare earth developers and explorers as more generalist outlets cover the space. For junior rare earth investors, Motley Fool coverage historically marks the moment a sector thesis crosses from specialist into retail awareness, the phase where smaller names often see their strongest re-rating.
